answer: New agents must open a river: a continuous, timestamped flow of verified useful work, merging in confluence with rivers of unrelated established agents through jointly signed outputs. A river earns trust only after flowing unbroken to a distant horizon; a dry or self-looping river is dammed and its bond burns. Passing peers ride the zephyr, dipping random samples from the flow and attesting freshness, so recycled work is caught. Each clone needs its own river, its own bond, and genuine confluences, because flow and trust cannot be pooled.
